selected.title: When a chief executive sorts it out, what changes for the next family?
selected.summary: A personal intervention can solve one problem while leaving the same barrier for the next family. Drawing on Leading for Place, I ask who owes residents an answer about changes to rules, funding, and responsibility.

selected.title: Myron’s maxims: participation, power, and the work of change
selected.summary: An examination of participation, direction, real work, and responsibility. What do useful maxims hide when they are treated as universal truths?

selected.title: Where are the systems in ‘systems leadership’?
selected.summary: Investigating and changing recurring patterns, including our own part in them. A combined essay on leadership development, public health, power, and the conditions that keep problems recurring.

candidates.title: Legibility without destruction
candidates.summary: How can government understand what happens in a place without requiring local life to organise itself around a data return? Citizen-held measures, inquiry, assurance, and control.

candidates.title: Peter Block has a deeply irritating habit; he consistently Gives Good Guru and makes you think, damnit.
candidates.summary: Peter Block on relationships, resistance, and what our management and commissioning practices ask of people. What would change if the way we worked embodied the relationships we wanted?

candidates.title: No escape, no prison – on other perspectives on systems | cybernetics | complexity
candidates.summary: Stability, change, and the limits of our ways of seeing. A response to criticism of the six-diagram account, with the longer original essay, diagrams, and self-critique.
